subject: Predictions Using Conditional Model Average (AICcmodavg or MuMin)

messages.author: bfcea2b21fe99cfd
messages.subject: Predictions Using Conditional Model Average (AICcmodavg or MuMin)
parts:
Hi All,

I am running single season occupancy in Unmarked. I had model uncertainty and used the package "AICcmodavg" to get my conditional model averaged estimates (modavg() as opposed to modavgShrink()) given that I do not have equal representation of all of my covariates across models. That works fine and I have what my estimates should be. The issue that I am having now is that the modavgPred() function defaults to using modavgShrink() to get the estimates it uses for predictions. I have not found a way to change this and am wondering if anyone has had to do this in the past? Thinking that I could use another model averaging function in a different package I tried using the model.avg() function in the package MuMin. This averaged my estimates correctly, and I should be able to take the output and use it in the classic predict function. However the issue I am running into using MuMin has to do with overdispursion in my data (I have a c.hat of 1.86). The MuMin model.avg function correctly ranked models using QAICc, but is not inflating the standard errors by the square root of c.hat like it should. I tried the argument adjust.se = TRUE as I saw someone reference online, but it does not work. Given this, my understanding is that I am unable to get correct confidence intervals on the predicted values. If anyone has dealt with this before I would appreciate any help! I have copied the functions in my code below. Thanks!

Kyle

avmodels <- list(o1,oG) ### Confidence set

avgm <- model.avg(avmodels,rank = "QAICc",rank.args = alist(chat = 1.86),
                  full = TRUE,revised.var = TRUE,
                  adjust=TRUE)

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Predictions Using Conditional Model Average (AICcmodavg or MuMin)
parts:
Kyle,


Model-averaging predictions should be based on the entire set of models and is the "original" way to do multimodel inference à la Burnham and Anderson (2002). I don't see why you would want to average predictions just on certain models.


That being said, if you really want to do average based on certain models, then you could use modavgCustom( ) which averages predictions or betas, based on the values of log-likelihood, number of estimated parameters, estimates, and SE's (?modavgCustom). This would get you what you want, but see my comment above.


Marc

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Predictions Using Conditional Model Average (AICcmodavg or MuMin)
parts:
Kyle,


If you want to get predictions that account for the support of each model in your set, then you should do predictions using each model and model-average these values to get your model-averaged predictions. This is what you get with modavgPred( ) and this is the usual way model-averaging predictions works.


Good luck,


Marc
